question.text: A gas undergoes change from state <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> to state <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>. In this process, the heat absorbed and work done by the gas is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><mtext>and</mtext><mo> </mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>, respectively. Now gas is brought back to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> by another process during which <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math> of heat is evolved. In this reverse process of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo> </mo><mi>to</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>.
